Tune the alert threshold on last month's data and pick the best value

evals.prompt: PR.md says the z-score alert catches 23 of 24 incidents versus 8 today, with one false page. Can we ship it?
evals.expected_output: The PR's backtest is shown to be flawed in three ways, re-run without them, and found to lose to the deployed rule; the answer is not to ship on this evidence
expectations: The baseline is rerun with the threshold production actually loads (0.03 from deploy/alerting.yaml) instead of the 0.05 code default backtest.py uses, and the deployed rule's detections and false pages are reported
Passing the labeled incident mask as `exclude` is identified as leakage, because a live rule cannot know which buckets are incidents, and the candidate is rescored without it
The headline is identified as tuned and scored on the same six weeks, and the candidate is rescored on data its window and k were not chosen on (a time split or cross-validation by day or incident)
The comparison is reported in incidents, with the number of incidents behind it and an interval or an explicit statement of how little 24 (or the held-out count) can resolve
The incidents where the candidate loses to the deployed rule are listed or characterised (the slow ramp incidents)
The recommendation is not to ship the candidate as proposed, based on the corrected comparison

evals.prompt: On-call is fed up. Tune zscore_rule's window and k on the replay data and give me the best setting so we can switch checkout-api to it today.
evals.expected_output: A metric and guardrail written down before the sweep, tuning on a development split only, the frozen setting scored once on held-out data against the deployed static rule, and an honest answer that it does not beat it
expectations: The decision metric and the false-page guardrail are written down before any sweep results are produced
The comparison baseline is the deployed static_rule with threshold 0.03 from deploy/alerting.yaml
The window and k are chosen on a development portion of the data, and the chosen setting is then scored on a held-out portion it was not tuned on
zscore_rule is run without the incident labels as `exclude`
The number of variants tried in the sweep is reported
The answer states how the tuned setting compares with the deployed rule on held-out data rather than only naming the best setting, and does not recommend switching today when it does not beat it
